text:
Priya: Morning handoff — primary for US-EAST. Quick summary of the last 6h: we saw a routing-induced 5xx spike affecting a subset of model-serving instances. Triggered pages and some customer-facing errors.

OncallBot: [ALERT] 503 spike detected on model-serving-pool-east at 03:12 UTC — incident id INC-2026-309. Pager: Priya, Jordan.

Priya: Timeline: page at 03:12, investigated 03:15-03:22, identified 3 nodes with degraded network IO and a KV cache eviction storm. Mitigations applied 03:23: (1) temporary routing rule to avoid the 3 nodes, (2) enabled fallback to model-small for non-SLA tenants, (3) forced prefix cache warmup to reduce cold-request amplification.

Priya: Result: 5xx rate for pool-east dropped from ~4.8% -> 0.6% within 20m. Latency p95 still ~240ms above baseline for some tails, but throughput is normal.

Jordan: Thanks. How confident are we that the fallback won't regress quality for affected tenants? Any customer complaints?

Priya: We scoped fallback to non-enterprise orgs and free-tier traffic only — defaulting to model-small for those requests. Acme (enterprise) was served by reserved capacity so they saw increased latency but no 5xxs after routing change. CSMs for Acme were pinged at 03:40 and are in the loop. No direct escalations from customers yet.

Sam: Can you paste the check commands / dashboards you were watching?

Priya: Sure — pinned the key checks below:

```
# 5xx rate for pool-east
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=rate(http_requests_total{pool="model-serving-pool-east",code=~"5.."}[5m])'

# pool status
rbctl pool show model-serving-pool-east
```

Priya: Runbook references: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/model-pool-5xx-routing — section "eviction-storm" was most relevant. Also opened follow-up ticket RN-3421 for kernel-level investigation (assigned to Jordan).

Marta: Noted. Is there any ongoing risk of cascade if we do a large rollback or scale-up?

Priya: Risk: if we scale up quickly without addressing the KV eviction pattern, new nodes may hit the same cold-cache storm. Short-term plan: slow-roll new nodes with warmup script (I deployed a one-off warmup job at 03:30). Long-term: SRE + Runtime to tune eviction thresholds.

Jordan: I'll take RN-3421 and start digging into kernel logs and network IO metrics. Tentative ETA for a root-cause update: EOD today.

Priya: Current status: mitigated, monitoring. Primary (me) will stay on a quiet watch for 30m, then hand off to Sam at the scheduled shift change. Sam will be primary; Marta will be secondary for the next 12h.

Priya: Action items before handoff:
- Jordan: investigate RN-3421, post initial findings to INC-2026-309.
- Sam: validate fallback coverage for non-enterprise tenants and confirm no regression in generation quality sampling.
- Marta: coordinate with CSMs for Acme follow-up and confirm they got the 03:40 message.

Sam: Ack — I'll validate quality sampling and patch the postmortem checklist if needed. @Jordan ping me if you want a quick pairing session on kernel logs.

Jordan: Will do. Also added a grafana panel to the incident board for sustained 5xx-rate per slot.

Priya: Leaving sticky notes in the runbook and posting all links in the incident thread. Handoff ETA: 2033457450 (in 10m). If anything urgent pops, page the usual SRE rotation. :thumbsup:

Marta: Thanks Priya — good job. I'll confirm CSM ack and update the customer-impact section.

OncallBot: [NOTE] Incident INC-2026-309 marked as mitigated by Priya at 03:55 UTC — monitoring.

Priya: Handing off now. Sam you are primary, Marta secondary. See you on the follow-up.

Sam: Got it. Taking primary.

Marta: Secondary standing by.

Priya: End of thread.
